flashcards.q: What determines a Docker build layer's cache key?
flashcards.a: Hash of the instruction text plus the upstream layer's cache key, plus (for COPY/ADD) a content hash of the copied files. Any upstream change cascades and invalidates everything downstream.

flashcards.q: Why put dependency-manifest COPY + install before COPY of the full source tree?
flashcards.a: So a source-only change doesn't invalidate and rerun the (slow) dependency install layer — cache keys chain from upstream, so ordering least-to-most-volatile maximizes reuse.

flashcards.q: What does BuildKit's --mount=type=cache do, and does its content end up in the final image?
flashcards.a: Mounts a persistent directory (e.g. pip/npm/go-mod cache) into a RUN step across builds on the same builder. Never becomes part of any image layer — it's excluded from the layer diff entirely.

flashcards.q: Why is ARG/ENV wrong for passing secrets into a Docker build?
flashcards.a: The value gets written into that layer permanently; even deleting it in a later layer only masks it in the merged view (via an overlay2 whiteout) — the earlier layer with the secret is still retrievable via docker history or by extracting the layer tarball.

flashcards.q: What's the fix for secrets during Docker build instead of ARG/ENV?
flashcards.a: BuildKit --mount=type=secret,id=<id> — mounts the secret file only for the duration of that RUN step, never written to any layer.

flashcards.q: Roughly how much does distroless cut CVE surface versus a full-distro base, and why?
flashcards.a: ~90% (Google's figure) — because most flagged CVEs live in OS packages (shell, package manager, coreutils) the application never touches, and distroless removes all of them.

flashcards.q: Distroless container is misbehaving in prod and has no shell. How do you debug it?
flashcards.a: kubectl debug -it <pod> --image=busybox --target=<container> — attaches an ephemeral debug container sharing the target's process namespace, without modifying the running image.

flashcards.q: Alpine vs distroless/glibc-slim for a Python service with native C-extension dependencies — which risk does Alpine carry?
flashcards.a: Alpine uses musl libc; wheels built against glibc (numpy, cryptography, many ML libs) can fail to install or silently fall back to a slow source compile. Use a glibc-based distroless/slim base instead.

flashcards.q: Difference between image scanning and image signing?
flashcards.a: Scanning answers 'what known-vulnerable software is in this image' (content). Signing (cosign/Sigstore) answers 'was this built by the trusted process and untampered since' (provenance/integrity). Neither substitutes for the other.

flashcards.q: Why does registry re-scanning matter even if build-time scanning already passed?
flashcards.a: CVE databases update independently of your build cadence — an image clean on Monday can have a critical finding by Friday with zero code changes, because a new CVE was published against an already-baked-in package version.

flashcards.q: When did BuildKit become Docker's default builder, and what changed mechanically?
flashcards.a: Docker 23.0, May 2023. Changed from a strictly sequential instruction-by-instruction builder to a DAG scheduler that runs independent stages in parallel and supports --mount=type=cache/secret as first-class primitives.

flashcards.q: Multi-arch image built on an arm64 laptop deployed to amd64 nodes without --platform — what happens?
flashcards.a: "exec format error" — the kernel can't execute a binary compiled for a different instruction set. Fix: docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 --push to produce a multi-arch manifest.
